A Physics‐Informed Two‐Stage Retrieval Method for EMIT Remote Sensing Methane Plumes
nodes.venue: Journal of Geophysical Research: Atmospheres
nodes.abstract: Abstract Hyperspectral satellite missions, particularly EMIT, have revolutionized methane point source monitoring. However, current operational retrieval pipelines typically rely on physically‐based matched filters followed by labor‐intensive manual verification to mitigate high false alarm rates caused by complex background interference. This dependence on human intervention restricts the scalability and efficiency required for rapid, automated global monitoring. To address these limitations, this paper proposes Plume‐Net, a novel Physics‐Informed Guided Two‐Stage Retrieval Method. Unlike conventional approaches, Plume‐Net decouples the task into a “global existence classification” stage and a “local pixel‐level regression” stage to maximize reliability without human‐in‐the‐loop. The core innovation lies in the integration of physical priors with deep learning: In the first stage, a Physics‐Informed Spectral Gating (PISG) module explicitly injects methane spectral absorption knowledge into the network, dynamically recalibrating channel weights to suppress background noise. In the second stage, to overcome the difficulties of regressing sparse, long‐tail plume distributions, we propose a Plume‐Focused Sampling Strategy and an Intensity‐Aware Pixel‐Level Weighted Loss function, forcing the network to prioritize rare but critical high‐concentration signals. Evaluated on real‐world EMIT observations, Plume‐Net achieves an ROC‐AUC of 0.961 in detection and a Mean Absolute Error (MAE) of 33.33 ppm·m in quantification. By significantly reducing false positives while maintaining high precision, this method offers a robust, fully automated alternative to current semi‐manual retrieval workflows.

nodes.name: Warming up ground-state orbitals: A route to excitation energies?
nodes.venue: The Journal of Chemical Physics
nodes.abstract: Linear-response time-dependent density functional theory (TDDFT) is the workhorse of spectral prediction, yet it can struggle to predict or even describe important low-lying excitation energies. An alternative is to use static formalisms to target excited-state energies directly from variational density functional theory (DFT). This may involve using custom excited-state functionals or feeding excited-state orbitals and densities into standard ground-state approximations, and can often be effective, even for describing states for which adiabatic TDDFT fails. However, this comes at the cost of requiring specialized algorithms to find stationary points. In this exploratory work, we demonstrate that finite-temperature DFT can provide an effective auxiliary framework for generating excited-state-like orbitals from ground-state orbitals for modern ensemble and state-specific functionals, such as the GX24 ground-state (G) and excited-state (X) functional. Notably, the necessary fixed-point algorithms are already available and well optimized in many electronic-structure codes.

nodes.name: Lightweight event recognition framework for Φ-OTDR systems with space-frequency fusion based on self-exclusion relational knowledge distillation
nodes.venue: Applied Optics
nodes.abstract: Phase-sensitive optical time-domain reflectometry (Φ-OTDR) systems are widely utilized in large-scale perimeter security and critical infrastructure protection. However, disturbance signal classification in Φ-OTDR systems heavily relies on complex model structures. Achieving high classification accuracy often requires high computational demands and substantial costs. This paper proposes an ultra-lightweight classification framework named space-frequency self-exclusion relational knowledge distillation (SF-SERKD). This framework constructs a three-channel feature map by using the short-time Fourier transform (STFT) combined with gradient analysis to capture the frequency-domain and spatial mutation features of signals. In addition, the framework introduces an innovative self-exclusion relational knowledge distillation (SERKD) strategy, which explicitly excludes the target sample’s own teacher features during the nearest-neighbor matching process. This strategy forces the student model to abandon feature alignment with high-noise samples or isolated samples, thereby reconstructing a robust and shared intra-class feature structure. Validation results in two different scenarios show that the student model achieves classification accuracies of 99.81% and 99.29%, alongside ultra-low nuisance alarm rates of 0.0004 and 0.0037, respectively, while only requiring 0.007M parameters. Notably, the accuracy of the student model in the second scenario is 1.87% higher than that of the teacher network. These results elucidate the effectiveness and generalization of the proposed method for real-time vibration event recognition in Φ-OTDR systems.

nodes.name: STLFM-based integration of sensing and secure communication in optical fiber
nodes.venue: Optics Express
nodes.abstract: Integrated sensing and communication in optical fiber (ISAC-OF) provides a promising solution for innovative applications such as smart cities, intelligent transportation, and ocean monitoring. However, dedicated sensing waveforms may increase the observability of optical links and introduce additional physical-layer security risks. In this paper, we propose and experimentally demonstrate an integrated sensing and secure communication scheme for optical fiber links. Quantum noise stream cipher (QNSC) is used to protect the confidentiality of payload symbols, while a symmetric triangular linear frequency modulation (STLFM) waveform is reused as a training sequence for communication and as a probing waveform for distributed sensing. QNSC inherently introduces a transmission penalty due to ciphertext constellation expansion. Compared with a repeated-QPSK training sequence reference, STLFM provides more accurate and stable frame-start estimation and more effective frequency offset compensation (FOC), thereby reducing receiver impairments and improving signal recovery. In a 200 Gbit/s, 100 km simulation, the proposed scheme achieves a received-power gain of 1.49 dB at the 7% HD-FEC threshold compared with a repeated-QPSK training sequence reference. In a 10 Gbit/s, 10.1 km proof-of-concept experiment, a received-power gain of 1 dB is obtained under the same threshold. The eavesdropper bit error rate (BER), together with the number of masked signals (NMS) and detection failure probability (DFP) evaluations, indicates that quantum noise masking increases ciphertext-state ambiguity and enhances payload confidentiality. For sensing, the scheme reconstructs distributed vibration signals along the 10.1 km fiber and achieves a spatial resolution of 3.9 m and a strain resolution of 22.37 n ε / H z . These results show that secure communication and distributed vibration sensing can be jointly realized over the same fiber link, while the shared STLFM waveform improves signal recovery.

nodes.name: TyphoonSat: A high-resolution satellite imagery dataset for tropical cyclone detection in the Northwest Pacific (2015–2024)
nodes.venue: Scientific Data
nodes.abstract: Abstract Tropical cyclones (TCs) in the Northwest Pacific pose significant threats to coastal regions, yet the lack of a standardized object-detection dataset hinders fair algorithm evaluation. We present TyphoonSat, a high-resolution satellite imagery dataset for TC detection spanning 2015–2024. It comprises 5390 Himawari-8/9 infrared cloud images (1601 × 1201 pixels, 5 km resolution) covering 100°E–180°E and 0°–60°N, with 7895 bounding-box annotations in YOLO format, derived from best-track records from the China Meteorological Administration (CMABST). The dataset supports coarse (all intensities regarded as one category) and fine-grained (six intensity levels) detection tasks. Benchmarks using YOLOv8 variants demonstrate strong performance for coarse detection (mAP@50 up to 0.923, CSI up to 0.791) and highlight challenges in distinguishing weak-to-moderate intensities, while SuperTY detection excels (CSI up to 0.609). This dataset provides a unified benchmark for TC detection and fosters advances in deep-learning-based meteorological remote sensing.

nodes.name: Seeing ahead through a state-of-the-art review of visual perception and predictive intelligence for collaborative robots
nodes.venue: Artificial Intelligence Review
nodes.abstract: Abstract The rate at which collaborative robots (cobots) are evolving from isolated, pre-programmed manipulators into collaborative partners that operate productively alongside humans, other robots, and machines is accelerating rapidly. Advances in computer vision is enabling cobots, even in dynamic and cluttered settings, to detect, recognise and assess both environment and actions. However, achieving higher detection accuracy and real-time localization in dynamic systems remains a challenge, as most existing approaches assume uncluttered backgrounds with limited scene complexity. Closing this gap is critical for both research and industrial deployment. This paper reviews the development of visual perception in cobots, surveys emerging computer vision algorithms, and examines a holistic perception pipeline in which raw vision signals, vision language models (VLMs), and augmented/virtual reality interfaces jointly power a unified sense-think-act loop. The review finds that cobots in high-mix, reconfigurable factories face serious challenges: occlusions in fields of view, fluctuating illumination, ambiguous backgrounds, few- or zero-shot object scenarios, high-speed motion, and computational problems in fusing heterogeneous data streams in real time. Cobots also need to manipulate damaged items, requiring vision algorithms that infer geometry from sparse cues and support adaptive grasping. Finally, the review identifies three complementary research directions to unlock plug-and-play cobots: (1) information aware sensor-fusion pipelines transmitting only credible voxels to reduce bandwidth while preserving sub-millimetre accuracy; (2) language conditioned planning and control networks mapping plain-language goals to smooth, jerk-bounded trajectories; and (3) pre-trained few-shot reward heads that score task progress without bespoke metrics, closing the reinforcement learning (RL) loop. Combined, these advances promise cobots that can be commissioned with relatively few demonstrations.

nodes.name: Multimodal modeling of the ictal onset zone in refractory insular epilepsy and seizure outcome of magnetic resonance‐guided laser interstitial therapy: A pediatric single‐center retrospective study
nodes.venue: Epilepsia
nodes.abstract: Abstract Objective This study was undertaken to evaluate seizure outcomes after magnetic resonance‐guided laser interstitial thermal therapy (MRgLITT) in children with insular epilepsy and to assess how the extent of ablation overlaps with multimodal definitions of the ictal onset zone (IOZ). Methods We conducted a retrospective, single‐center study including consecutive pediatric patients treated with MRgLITT for insular epilepsy. All patients underwent presurgical evaluation including electroencephalography (EEG) and magnetic resonance imaging (MRI); fluorodeoxyglucose positron emission tomography (FDG‐PET) and stereo‐EEG (SEEG) were performed in negative‐MRI cases. Epileptic zone was identified by visual analysis of SEEG recording. Postablation contrast‐enhancing volumes were manually segmented and coregistered with IOZ estimates derived from Multi‐centre Epilepsy Lesion Detection (MELD) MRI analysis, FDG‐PET voxel‐based analysis, and the Epileptogenicity Index, when available. Spatial concordance between modalities was assessed using Dice similarity coefficients, and the proportion of each IOZ modality encompassed within the ablation volume was correlated with postoperative seizure outcomes (International League Against Epilepsy classification). Results Eight children (median age = 10.4 years, range = 2.3–17) were included, with a median postoperative follow‐up of 38 months. Two patients had insular tumors, and both achieved seizure freedom after complete ablation. Among the six MRI‐negative patients, FDG‐PET revealed insular hypometabolism in four, MELD detected a median of one insular cluster (range 1–3), and SEEG identified focal insular ictal activity in three cases. Overall, four negative‐MRI patients achieved seizure freedom: three after MRgLITT alone and one after MRgLITT combined with frontal opercular resection. One transient postoperative aphasia was observed. Intermodality spatial concordance was low across all comparisons. A greater proportion of FDG‐PET hypometabolism included in the ablation volume was associated with better seizure outcomes ( p = .012). Significance MRgLITT is an effective and safe treatment option for focal insular epilepsy in children, either as standalone therapy or in a combined approach. Optimal outcome depends on accurate preoperative delineation of the IOZ and its complete ablation.

nodes.name: Model Pembelajaran MordiScVeIn Berbasis Multimodal Digital Interaktif untuk Meningkatkan Berpikir Kritis dan Hasil Belajar Siswa pada Pembelajaran IPAS Sekolah Dasar
nodes.venue: Jurnal Pendidikan dan Pembelajaran Indonesia (JPPI)
nodes.abstract: Penelitian ini bertujuan untuk menganalisis peningkatan kemampuan berpikir kritis dan hasil belajar siswa melalui penerapan model pembelajaran MordiScVeIn berbasis multimodal digital interaktif pada pembelajaran Ilmu Pengetahuan Alam dan Sosial (IPAS), khususnya materi Perubahan Wujud Benda di sekolah dasar. Penelitian menggunakan metode mixed methods dengan desain explanatory sequential, yang mengintegrasikan analisis data kuantitatif dan pendalaman temuan melalui data kualitatif. Penelitian melibatkan kelas eksperimen dan kelas kontrol. Data dikumpulkan melalui tes pretest dan posttest, observasi, wawancara, dan dokumentasi. Analisis kuantitatif dilakukan menggunakan statistik deskriptif, N-Gain, dan uji-t, sedangkan data kualitatif dianalisis secara deskriptif. Hasil penelitian menunjukkan bahwa rata-rata posttest kelas eksperimen mencapai 85,37, lebih tinggi daripada kelas kontrol sebesar 72,43, dengan selisih 12,94 poin. Hasil uji-t menunjukkan adanya perbedaan yang signifikan antara kedua kelas ((t(58)=6,88); (p<0,001)). Selain itu, nilai N-Gain sebesar 0,675 menunjukkan peningkatan pada kategori sedang. Distribusi nilai setelah pembelajaran menunjukkan bahwa 25 siswa (83,33%) berada pada kategori tinggi dan 5 siswa (16,67%) pada kategori sedang. Temuan ini menunjukkan bahwa penerapan model MordiScVeIn berbasis multimodal digital interaktif berpotensi mendukung peningkatan hasil belajar dan kemampuan berpikir kritis siswa dalam pembelajaran IPAS. Model ini dapat menjadi alternatif pembelajaran yang memadukan aktivitas penemuan, penyelidikan, verifikasi, dan inovasi dengan berbagai media digital interaktif.

nodes.name: Integrating Agrometeorology, Agronomy and Artificial Intelligence for Climate-Resilient Sustainable Food Production: A Critical Narrative Review
nodes.venue: Journal of Experimental Agriculture International
nodes.abstract: Climate-resilient food production requires decisions that are meteorologically informed, agronomically plausible and adaptive to rapidly changing conditions. Agrometeorology provides observations and forecasts of weather and climate risk; agronomy translates those risks into crop, soil and management responses; and artificial intelligence can fuse high-volume, heterogeneous data, learn complex relationships and accelerate prediction. These domains are increasingly connected, yet their evidence bases remain partly fragmented. This critical narrative review evaluates how their integration can support sustainable crop production, with particular attention to the chain from environmental observation and prediction to management action and measurable resilience outcomes. Literature published from 1 January 2000 to 8 August 2026 was examined through relevant agricultural, multidisciplinary and biomedical scholarly sources, with supplementary citation searching and verification of bibliographic metadata. The synthesis shows that the strongest case for integration is not a replacement of process knowledge by data-driven prediction, but a division of labour: meteorological models define time-varying hazard, agronomic models constrain biological plausibility and management options, and artificial intelligence improves data fusion, bias correction, pattern recognition and computational efficiency. Evidence is comparatively mature for remote sensing, yield prediction and process-based crop modelling, and is rapidly advancing for machine-learned weather prediction. By contrast, end-to-end demonstrations that connect forecast skill to farm decisions, yield stability, resource-use efficiency, profitability and environmental outcomes remain limited. Hybrid crop-model and machine-learning approaches are promising, but uncertainty calibration, domain shift, sparse ground truth, interoperability, digital inequality and data governance remain substantial constraints. Digital twins offer a useful integration architecture, although agricultural implementations are still less mature than the concept implies. Future research should prioritise multi-environment prospective validation, decision-centred forecast verification, causal evaluation of management recommendations, uncertainty-aware hybrid modelling and equitable deployment. The most defensible conclusion is that integration can improve climate resilience only when predictive accuracy is coupled to agronomic actionability, transparent uncertainty and outcome-based evaluation.

nodes.name: Enhanced Convolutional Neural Network Architecture with Attention-Guided Feature Refinement for Robust Image Classification
nodes.venue: International Journal of Drug Delivery Technology
nodes.abstract: Image classification remains a foundational problem in computer vision, underpinning applications that range from medical diagnostics to autonomous navigation. Although deep convolutional neural networks (CNNs) have substantially advanced classification accuracy over the last decade, standard architectures such as VGG, ResNet, and plain CNNs often struggle to jointly optimize accuracy, parameter efficiency, and robustness to intra-class variation. This paper proposes an AttentionGuided Refinement Network (AGR-Net), a CNN architecture that integrates a lightweight channel-and-spatial attention module with residual feature refinement blocks to improve discriminative feature learning while maintaining a compact parameter footprint. The proposed model is evaluated on the CIFAR-10 benchmark dataset using a rigorous experimental protocol that includes data augmentation, learning-rate scheduling, and five-fold cross-validation. Comparative experiments against baseline architectures, including a plain CNN, VGG-16, ResNet-18, and MobileNetV2, demonstrate that AGR-Net achieves a top-1 accuracy of 94.6%, outperforming the strongest baseline by 1.8 percentage points while using 27% fewer parameters than ResNet-18. Ablation studies confirm that the attention module and refinement blocks each contribute measurably to the accuracy gain. The results indicate that attention-guided refinement offers a favorable trade-off between accuracy, efficiency, and robustness, making the proposed architecture suitable for deployment in resource-constrained and real-time image classification systems. The paper further discusses the advantages, practical applications, limitations, and future research directions of the proposed approach.

nodes.name: International Journal of Drug Delivery Technology
Effect of hierarchical prompt engineering on convolutional neural networks generated by large language models for helmet wearing compliance classification
nodes.venue: Discover Artificial Intelligence
nodes.abstract: Abstract Non-compliance with Personal Protective Equipment (PPE) use regulations, particularly helmet wearing, remains a critical occupational safety challenge in high-risk industrial environments. This study investigates how hierarchical prompt engineering shapes the quality of Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) generated by Large Language Models (LLMs) for image-level helmet-wearing compliance classification (helmet vs. no-helmet) as a mechanism for PPE compliance monitoring. Four LLMs (ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini, and Grok) produced executable PyTorch scripts across three prompt tiers of increasing specificity. These configurations were evaluated over 20 independent runs on a purpose-built dataset of 972 balanced images, using six classification metrics, four prompt quality metrics, and three resource efficiency dimensions. Ten of the twelve configurations converged to a high-performance plateau (accuracy 0.957-−0.967, AUC 0.985-−0.993). Claude at Tier 1 achieved the highest accuracy (0.967) and the lowest CPU usage (12.2%), whereas the best-calibrated (lowest-loss) pipelines were produced by Gemini and Grok at Tier 1 (test loss 0.127 and 0.142), reflecting an accuracy–calibration dissociation that we analyze in detail. However, Gemini and Grok experienced catastrophic convergence failures at Tier 3 (accuracy $$\approx $$ 0.58), revealing that over-specification of architectural and training constraints can destabilize CNN generation even when the produced scripts are syntactically valid. Higher prompt specificity does not consistently improve accuracy or validity rate. Instead, LLM identity interacts strongly with the prompt tier and emerges as a more critical factor than prompt design alone, although each LLM–tier condition is represented by a single generated script. Within the scope of this controlled, image-level evaluation, basic and structured prompting represent the recommended operating range for developing PPE compliance classifiers, delivering competitive accuracy and full validity rate across all models without the convergence failures observed at Tier 3. Validation in real industrial settings remains necessary.

nodes.name: Cross-Omics correlation and genomic pattern recognition for accurate tumor detection in oncological surgery decision-making
nodes.venue: Discover Computing
nodes.abstract: Abstract A genomic sequence analysis is necessary to determine the cancer-specific genomic patterns for oncological surgery decision-making. However, the existing works overlooked the cross-omics interaction regarding Genomic Pattern Recognition (GPR). Therefore, Chebyshev-Excoffier Heun Density-Based Spatial Clustering of Application with Noise (CEHDBSCAN)-based GPR and Cross-Omics Correlation Analysis (COCA) using Heaviside Function-based Pearson Correlation Coefficient (HeFPCC) is proposed. Primarily, the patient registers on the hospital’s server. Then, the multi-omics data is collected and then encrypted using Legendre Chi Function-based Advanced Encryption Standard (LCFAES). Further, in the hospital server, the secured multi-omics data is decrypted and pre-processed. Afterward, the CEHDBSCAN-based GPR is performed. Then, the features are extracted, and the hidden mutation progress is analyzed using Jacobi Elliptic Function-Hidden Markov Model (JEFHMM). Also, the HeFPCC-based COCA is carried out. Meanwhile, the extracted features are selected using Hawk Fish Walsh Function Optimization Algorithm (HFWaFOA). Finally, the gradients are secured using Differential Privacy (DP); then, the tumor is detected using Deep Shifted and Scaled Sigmoid Alpha Dropout Learning Neural Network (DSSSADLNN). The classified output is further given for decision-making regarding oncological surgery. Thus, the proposed framework effectively recognized the genomic pattern and classified the tumor with an accuracy of 99.05%, showing better performance than existing works.

nodes.name: Comprehensive Analytical Study on Spatial Reasoning and Adaptation of Human Brain Versus Artificial Intelligence - A Review Report
nodes.venue: International Journal of Innovative Science and Research Technology
nodes.abstract: Recent advances in computer vision, spatial computing, robotics, and embodied artificial intelligence (AI) have substantially improved machine capabilities in visual perception, navigation, spatial reasoning, and object manipulation. However, performance on structured benchmarks and controlled environments does not necessarily demonstrate equivalence to human spatial intelligence in complex real-world situations. This review examines whether current AI systems can reproduce the breadth and flexibility of human spatial and embodied intelligence, with particular emphasis on their implications for the potential replacement of humans by AI. The review synthesizes theoretical and empirical literature on human spatial cognition, embodied AI, vision-language-action models, robotics, and relevant AI capability benchmarks. The evidence is organised around four dimensions: (1) biological sensorimotor coupling and proprioception, (2) zero-shot spatial problem-solving and dynamic affordance recognition, (3) physical common-sense reasoning and adaptation, and (4) energy-efficient and context-sensitive spatial processing. Existing research indicates that AI systems have achieved considerable progress in perception, navigation, planning, and manipulation, but continue to encounter challenges involving unfamiliar environments, occlusion, uncertainty, dynamic obstacles, changing object configurations, physical interaction, long-horizon adaptation, and generalisation beyond training distributions. Human spatial intelligence, in contrast, integrates perception, proprioception, embodied experience, contextual knowledge, physical intuition, memory, and flexible real-time decision-making as an interconnected system. The reviewed evidence therefore suggests that current AI can augment and extend human spatial capabilities but cannot yet reproduce the breadth, adaptability, embodied experience, and contextual flexibility of human spatial intelligence. Spatial ability consequently represents an important dimension of human irreplaceability and supports a future paradigm of human–AI complementarity rather than complete human substitution.

nodes.name: International Journal of Innovative Science and Research Technology
CORA-CSS: Correlation-Aware Reputation and Influence-Capped Fusion for Collusion-Resilient Cooperative Spectrum Sensing
nodes.venue: International Journal of Scientific Research in Computer Science, Engineering and Information Technology
nodes.abstract: Cooperative spectrum sensing improves primary-user detection through spatial diversity, but collaborative fusion also creates an attack surface: multiple Byzantine radios can coordinate their reports so that individually plausible observations become collectively dominant. Existing reputation methods attenuate persistently unreliable radios, while SENTRY-CSS combines adaptive reliability with selective re-sensing; however, protected reference labels and arbitrary collusion remain important limitations. This paper introduces CORA-CSS, a reference-free fusion method that combines a rolling residual-correlation graph, consensus-based reputation, and a sublinear group-influence cap. Each radio is scored against the instantaneous robust median, its reputation is updated from agreement history, and radios exhibiting strongly correlated residuals with sustained deviation receive a multiplicative influence cap before soft fusion. A reproducible Monte Carlo study models twelve heterogeneous sensing radios, fading-like sensing variation, noise uncertainty, primary occupancy imbalance, and four attack families. In the main ten-seed condition with four colluding Byzantine radios, CORA-CSS achieves 0.9659±0.0100 balanced accuracy, 0.9677±0.0103 detection probability, 0.0358±0.0125 false-alarm probability, and 0.9515±0.0145 F1. Reference-free reputation without the correlation cap reaches 0.9454 balanced accuracy, while equal-soft, median, majority, trimmed-mean, and clean-calibrated SVM fusion degrade substantially. CORA-CSS remains above 0.96 balanced accuracy with four colluders in the attacker-count sweep and retains useful performance with five. A stress test also exposes the boundary of the method: under weak stealth attacks that preserve plausible independent-looking reports, ordinary equal-soft fusion can outperform CORA-CSS. The contribution is therefore a collusion-focused robustness mechanism, not a universal replacement for conventional fusion.

nodes.name: International Journal of Scientific Research in Computer Science, Engineering and Information Technology
Automated Motorsport Adjudication: Rule-Conditioned Vision-Language Models for High-Frequency Telemetry Analysis
nodes.venue: International Journal of Creative and Open Research in Engineering and Management
nodes.abstract: The automation of operational stewarding in high-speed motorsports traditionally relies on resource-intensive video tracking algorithms, which introduce severe latency, synchronization friction, and computational overhead. This paper proposes a novel Time-Series Vision-Language Model framework that bypasses spatial video processing entirely by employing a Chart-as-Image methodology. By ingesting high-frequency 20 hertz Formula 1 telemetry data via the FastF1 interface, the system deterministically isolates four-second temporal anomaly windows and renders standardized four-channel multi-variate plots encompassing velocity, throttle application, braking state, and engine revolutions per minute. These visual artifacts are subsequently evaluated by a frontier Vision-Language Model conditioned on the 2026 Federation Internationale de l Automobile Section B Sporting Regulations via an in-memory Retrieval-Augmented Generation pipeline utilizing normalized inner-product vector search. To ensure operational reliability, each generated Chain-of-Thought verdict is validated against a deterministic heuristic baseline and a three-factor hallucination guardrail prior to presentation within a human-in-the-loop adjudication interface. Empirical evaluation across a curated register of seventeen historical motorsport incidents across seven circuits demonstrates high diagnostic precision, near-zero structural hallucination, and substantial reductions in token consumption and adjudication latency compared to continuous video streams

nodes.name: International Journal of Creative and Open Research in Engineering and Management
A multimodal data-fusion model for 5-minute-ahead depth-of-anesthesia prediction using VitalDB: a retrospective study
nodes.venue: BMC Anesthesiology
nodes.abstract: Abstract Background Bispectral index (BIS) monitoring primarily assesses the current depth of anesthesia and does not indicate future trends. Predicting future low BIS may give anesthesiologists time to assess potentially excessive depth of anesthesia in advance and reduce unnecessary exposure to deep anesthesia. This study developed and validated a multimodal data-fusion model using VitalDB for 5-minute-ahead BIS prediction during the maintenance phase of intravenous anesthesia and evaluated its ability to provide early warning of BIS < 40. Methods We selected 2,407 surgical cases from VitalDB and integrated BIS monitoring, vital signs, ventilation, and intravenous anesthetic medication data from the preceding 120 s during the maintenance phase of intravenous anesthesia with baseline clinical information to predict BIS at 300 s ahead. One window was generated every 120 s, and patients were assigned to the training and test sets at an approximately 75:25 ratio. A multimodal data-fusion model was developed using histogram-based gradient boosting (HGB) regression. The primary evaluation metric was mean absolute error (MAE). Observed 5-minute-ahead BIS < 40 was defined as the positive outcome for calculating the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUROC). Predicted BIS < 40 was used as the early-warning rule to calculate sensitivity, specificity, positive predictive value, and negative predictive value. Patient-level paired bootstrap resampling was used to estimate 95% confidence intervals, and SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) analysis was used to assess feature contributions. Results The MAE was 4.61 for the multimodal data-fusion model and 4.79 for BIS monitoring-only HGB, a relative reduction of 3.9%; the paired reduction was 0.19 (95% confidence interval: 0.16–0.22). With predicted BIS < 40 as the early-warning rule, the multimodal data-fusion model achieved an AUROC of 0.841, sensitivity of 67.8%, specificity of 83.4%, positive predictive value of 73.5%, and negative predictive value of 79.2%. Conclusions In test data from the maintenance phase of intravenous anesthesia, the multimodal data-fusion model improved 5-minute-ahead BIS prediction and discrimination of BIS < 40 compared with the BIS monitoring-only HGB model. Its MAE and RMSE indicated better predictive performance than that reported in previous related studies.

nodes.name: Tree cover increases on agricultural land amid continued landscape-level deforestation: a case study from eastern Afghanistan
nodes.venue: Environmental Monitoring and Assessment
nodes.abstract: Understanding changes in tree cover within agricultural landscapes is critical for assessing the resilience of rural communities and consequent land use dynamics in conflict-affected regions. This study examines spatiotemporal land use and tree cover changes across four districts of Nangarhar Province in eastern Afghanistan using high-resolution (3 m/pixel) satellite imagery. The temporal window examined for this study (2016-2024) spans a period of significant geopolitical upheaval in Afghanistan, including the collapse of the republican government in 2021 and the resulting shift in political power and governance dynamics. An object-based image analysis framework combined with a support vector machine classifier was applied to map five land use classes within settlement areas: tree cover, cropland, water, built-up areas, and barren land. Classification accuracy was assessed using stratified random sampling and Cohen's kappa coefficient, with all maps achieving κ values above 0.80. Post-classification change detection and transition matrices were used to quantify class-to-class conversions in hectares, while Sankey diagrams were employed to visualise the magnitude and direction of land use transitions. The results reveal varying patterns of tree cover change across the study districts, with evidence of both tree cover gains linked to expansion of agroforestry and on-farm tree retention, and losses driven by agricultural expansion and development. These changes may influence local livelihoods, as trees on farms provide important resources such as fruit, fuelwood, and shade. The findings demonstrate the effectiveness of integrating high-resolution remote sensing, object-based classification, and Sankey-based visualisation for analysing complex land use dynamics.

nodes.name: Tracking crop evapotranspiration and water stress across seasons using multi-sensor UAV observations
nodes.venue: Biogeosciences
nodes.abstract: Abstract. Field-scale estimation of evapotranspiration (ET) using high-resolution data supports water conservation and yield optimization by enabling localized water use monitoring and early detection of crop stress. This study applies the Priestley–Taylor Two-Source Energy Balance (TSEB-PT) model at 15 cm resolution using unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) data over a 10-hectare field across three seasons: sugar beet (2021), potato (2022), and winter wheat (2023). Key inputs included thermal infrared (TIR) for land surface temperature (LST), multispectral (MS) and LiDAR data for canopy characterization, and a fusion of MS derived green area index (GAI) and LiDAR derived plant area index (PAI) to derive the fraction of green LAI (fg). Model outputs were validated against eddy covariance (EC) flux data using footprint modeling. Results showed high sensitivity to LST, emphasizing the importance of accurate thermal calibration. While both GAI and PAI provided comparable LAI inputs during peak growth, GAI better captured functional canopy decline during stress and senescence, especially in winter wheat, where dense structure led to cooling effects unrelated to transpiration. Dynamic fg improved ET accuracy across all crops, particularly under declining canopy function. Overall, TSEB-PT showed strong agreement with EC measurements (RMSE = 0.14 mm/h, R² = 0.49; R² = 0.81 excluding senescence). UAV TIR based ET maps also revealed early stress signals prior to changes in MS or LiDAR based metrics. This study demonstrates the value of integrating very-high-resolution UAV data with the TSEB-PT model for multi-crop and season-long ET monitoring and early stress detection.

nodes.name: Tracing locations from pixels: A survey of worldwide image geo-localization
nodes.venue: Information Processing & Management
nodes.abstract: Worldwide image geo-localization (WIGL) estimates the geographic coordinates of a photograph from its visual content, without metadata on the query image and without a known search area. This capability supports practical applications, including cybercrime source tracing, disaster response, and autonomous navigation. In this manuscript, a comprehensive review of WIGL is presented, in which current methods are systematically organized into four paradigms: classification-based, retrieval-based, generation-based, and retrieval-augmented generation (RAG). For each paradigm, representative approaches and core design principles are examined, with their strengths and limitations compared. Training, testing, and fine-tuning datasets are also reviewed in depth. A spatial distribution analysis of these datasets reveals notable coverage biases in existing benchmarks. Standard evaluation metrics are consolidated, and the reported results on six test sets are aggregated, providing a common basis for comparison across methods. The comparative analysis of reported results indicates that RAG approaches currently achieve the highest accuracy on major benchmarks, though this advantage is partly confounded by larger backbone models and training data while generation-based approaches offer a promising alternative for zero-shot location inference. Finally, several under-explored research challenges that are rarely discussed in prior surveys are identified and outlined. These include the difficulty of disambiguating visually similar images captured at distant locations, as well as other open problems to guide future work.

nodes.name: The riverine legacy of reservoirs
nodes.venue: Frontiers in Freshwater Science
nodes.abstract: Reservoirs exposed to similar environmental drivers frequently exhibit markedly different ecological responses. Existing reservoir concepts describe many aspects of impounded rivers, but none directly explains why environmental drivers produce contrasting ecological responses among reservoirs. I propose riverine legacy , defined as the enduring ecological characteristics that reservoirs inherit from the rivers they impound. Riverine legacy arises because impoundment transforms river systems without completely erasing their spatial, environmental, ecological, and trophic organization. Riverine legacy consists of five interconnected dimensions through which inherited characteristics interact with contemporary environmental drivers to generate ecological responses at population, community, and ecosystem levels. I provide three examples to illustrate how riverine legacy may explain contrasting responses to biological invasions, longitudinal variation in community organization, and differences in ecological transformation among impounded rivers. The concept yields six testable predictions concerning ecological organization, ecosystem responsiveness, fisheries, recovery trajectories, and conservation opportunities across reservoir networks. Riverine legacy is not proposed as a metric but as a concept that generates testable hypotheses about how inherited riverine characteristics influence contemporary ecological responses. Recognizing that reservoirs retain enduring ecological characteristics inherited from their riverine origins provides a foundation for improving ecological interpretation, conservation planning, monitoring, management, and restoration across impounded river systems.

nodes.name: Shelterbelts: A Python library for characterising farmland tree groups and their influence on nearby pasture and cropland
nodes.abstract: Shelterbelts is an open source Python library for mapping and categorising groups of trees in agricultural landscapes, and the corresponding shelter provided to nearby pixels based on the wind direction or density of tree cover. Starting from a binary tree raster, pixels are labelled into ecologically meaningful categories based on their structure and location including: scattered trees, forest core and edge, riparian and road buffers, other linear (windbreaks/tree-rows) and non-linear patches. The library also provides functions to fetch and transform raster datasets for wind speed and direction, elevation and topographic attributes, along with national road and hydroline vector datasets. The library can also be used to process LiDAR through crown delineation, or fetch and transform global canopy height and land cover data, and even to train a new annual model to predict tree cover from satellite imagery, to create the necessary input binary raster for the pipeline. The software was designed and tested on landscapes in Australia, but can be applied anywhere. It can be run locally in jupyter notebooks or at scale in high-throughput environments such as the National Computing Infrastructure (NCI). The github repository is available here. https://github.com/ChristopherBradley/shelterbelts Australia-wide map of shelterbelt classifications can be viewed at this Earth Engine App. https://christopher-bradley-phd.projects.earthengine.app/view/shelterbelts

nodes.name: Satellite Orbit Simulation to Support Sensor Calibration/Validation
nodes.venue: Digital Repository at the University of Maryland (University of Maryland College Park)
nodes.abstract: This presentation was shared at the in-person conference of the 2026 ESSIC/CISESS Summer Internship Program held on 19 August 2026. The slides were presented by David Liu, a student at Marriotts Ridge High School, under the mentorship of Yan Bai (UMD/ESSIC/CISESS), Dr. Xi Shao (UMD/ESSIC/CISESS), and Dr. Changyong Cao (NOAA). In this presentation, the intern examined satellite orbit prediction using Two-Line Element (TLE) data and the Simplified General Perturbations 4 (SGP4) propagation model, with attention to orbital perturbations and their effects on prediction accuracy. The study also compared Systems Tool Kit (STK), a high-fidelity aerospace analysis platform, with Zerua, a web-based orbital visualization tool, and applied Zerua to simulate satellites from the Joint Polar Satellite System (JPSS) and the six-satellite COSMIC-2 constellation. The simulations were used to visualize satellite orbits and support analysis of satellite positioning, overpasses, and coordinated observations relevant to sensor calibration and validation. This internship study provides an important foundation for future satellite orbit prediction and coordinated observation studies, contributing to advancements in environmental monitoring and the evaluation of Earth-observing satellite sensor data quality.

nodes.name: Digital Repository at the University of Maryland (University of Maryland College Park)
MSFANet: a multi-scale feature aggregation network for tobacco pest recognition
nodes.venue: Frontiers in Plant Science
nodes.abstract: Introduction Tobacco is a globally significant economic crop, and pest infestation represents one of the primary factors contributing to declines in both yield and quality. However, tobacco pests encompass a wide variety of species that differ substantially in morphology and scale. Field-captured images are frequently subject to complex background interference and class imbalance, presenting considerable challenges for automated recognition. Existing deep learning approaches remain limited in their capacity for multi-scale feature extraction and discriminative feature representation under such conditions. To address these challenges, this study proposes a Multi-Scale Feature Aggregation Network (MSFANet) for tobacco pest recognition, formulated here as a single-label image classification task. Methods To address scale variation and complex field backgrounds, two task-oriented modules were developed. The Multi-Scale Pyramid Pooling (MSPP) module aggregates contextual information across multiple receptive fields through parallel feature extraction and adaptive cross-branch fusion. The Hierarchical Feature Fusion Block (HFFB) subsequently refines the feature representations through spatial gating and partial convolution. An auxiliary classification head and Focal Loss were incorporated during training to provide intermediate supervision and address class imbalance, respectively. Results The effectiveness of MSFANet was evaluated on a dataset comprising 13 tobacco-associated pest and natural-enemy categories. The model achieved accuracy, precision, recall, and F1-score of 97.63%, 97.89%, 97.59%, and 97.71%, respectively, with a parameter count of 1.21 M. Among the models trained from random initialization, MSFANet shared the highest accuracy while using the fewest parameters. Discussion By combining multi-scale contextual aggregation with hierarchical feature refinement, MSFANet achieved accurate classification across the 13 tobacco-associated categories under complex field conditions. The proposed method provides effective technical support for automated and precision-oriented pest monitoring in tobacco fields, offering practical value for advancing precise pest management and the broader development of smart agriculture.

nodes.name: Leveraging satellite products and machine learning/deep learning models for the upgrading of agro-advisory systems in India: A bibliometric and systematic narrative review
nodes.venue: Plant Science Today
nodes.abstract: A comprehensive bibliometric review was conducted to evaluate the most relevant literature retrieved from the Scopus database, resulting in the identification of 125 relevant publications from an initial pool of 1948 records through a screening process based on the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA). The bibliometric analysis revealed a significant increasing trend in year-wise publications and citations, wherein India and the US emerged as the leading contributors with total publications of 34 and 25 respectively. Notably, the systematic narrative review highlights that agro-advisory systems (AAS) have increased farmer income by 83 %, improved crop yields by 6–25 % and enhanced farm profitability by 15–26 % in India. Despite these achievements, conventional AAS frameworks that rely predominantly on automatic weather stations (AWS) continue to face critical limitations, including sparse spatial coverage, restricted agro-meteorological observations, data discontinuities and inadequate representation of local microclimatic variability. To address these limitations, the study highlights the importance of integrating AWS observations with high-resolution satellite products through downscaling and subsequent assimilation within the Weather Research and Forecasting Data Assimilation (WRFDA) framework to improve the spatial accuracy of weather forecasts and facilitate the delivery of reliable block-level and village-level agro-advisories. However, the operational implementation of satellite-assisted weather forecasting using the Weather Research and Forecasting (WRF) model is often constrained by latency in data availability, as many high-resolution satellite products require several hours to multiple days for processing and dissemination. In order to overcome this limitation, the review further demonstrates the considerable potential of machine learning (ML) and deep learning (DL) models trained using historical satellite observations along with meteorological predictors derived from numerical weather prediction (NWP) systems for enhancing downscaling capabilities and improving forecast accuracy. The results inferred that the satellite-based weather forecasting using ML and DL architectures achieved strong predictive performance, with reported R² values of up to 0.982, 0.976 and 0.95 for rainfall, temperature and aerosol concentration respectively. These findings demonstrate the increasing potential of satellite-driven ML and DL approaches for high-resolution weather forecasting and their applicability to next-generation, location-specific agro-advisory services. However, their operational utilisation depends on the availability of adequate computational infrastructure, skilled human resources, economic feasibility, institutional coordination and farmer acceptance. Therefore, the future of satellite-based AAS lies in developing computationally efficient, economically viable and farmer centric decision support platforms capable of translating complex forecast information into timely, understandable and actionable recommendations for climate-resilient agriculture.

nodes.name: LLM4GIS: Methods, Applications, and Prospects
nodes.venue: ISPRS International Journal of Geo-Information
nodes.abstract: The rapid advancement of large language models (LLMs) offers new avenues for overcoming the limitations of current data-driven GIS analysis methods, giving rise to the emerging field of large language model-driven GIS analysis (LLM4GIS). This study presents a systematic review of 673 relevant research articles published between 2022 and July 2026. By tracing the five-stage evolutionary trajectory of GIS analysis methods and elaborating the framework for LLM4GIS, we conduct a quantitative bibliometric analysis that reveals the field’s rapid growth from sporadic exploration to explosive expansion, along with the shifting landscape of its dominant technical trajectories. Building on these analyses, we develop a taxonomy spanning four dimensions—technical approaches, datasets, applications, and evaluation—and systematically analyze the advances and evaluation methodologies across five core application areas: geospatial knowledge question answering, knowledge extraction, spatiotemporal reasoning, geospatial code generation, and analysis modeling. Key challenges and future research directions are further discussed along five dimensions: multimodal data integration, high-quality data development, domain-specific model development, integration of world models with real-world geospatial environments, and interpretability and trustworthiness. This review provides a systematic reference for advancing the bidirectional synergy between LLM4GIS and GIS4LLM and for fostering a new generation of spatiotemporal intelligence ecosystems.

nodes.name: Improved RT-DETR-based detection and counting of shrimp in EK80 acoustic echogram images
nodes.venue: Frontiers in Marine Science
nodes.abstract: Accurately detecting shrimp targets in EK80 acoustic echogram images is challenging due to their small size, high-density aggregation, and strong background clutter, which collectively hinder conventional object-detection models. To address these issues, we propose an enhanced detection framework based on RT-DETR. Our method introduces three key improvements: the integration of an Efficient Multi-Scale Attention (EMA) mechanism to strengthen feature representation, the addition of a dedicated P2 detection layer to better capture fine-grained information for small objects, and the adoption of a combined Focal Loss and Wise-IoU (WIoU) loss function to mitigate class imbalance and refine bounding-box regression. Experimental evaluations demonstrate that the improved model achieves a mean mAP@50 of 0.844 and a mean mAP@50–95 of 0.437, outperforming the baseline RT-DETR. Furthermore, by incorporating DeepSORT for multi-object tracking and identity association, the proposed system enables automated shrimp counting with an average accuracy of 83.32% across 10 video clips. These results demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed approach in enhancing detection, tracking, and enumeration performance in complex acoustic imagery, offering a promising technical solution for real-world applications such as intake safety monitoring and early warning systems at nuclear power plants.

nodes.name: Heterophily Limits Spatial Graph Encoding for PM2.5 Forecasting in IoT Smart Cities
nodes.venue: International journal of intelligent engineering and systems
nodes.abstract: Graph neural networks are widely assumed to improve air-quality forecasting as the spatial heterogeneity of Internet of Things monitoring networks grows.We test this on a reproducible four-network benchmark under identical preprocessing, comparing a temporal-only Transformer against three graph architectures, and we introduce a spatial heterophily index computable in advance.Across the three networks on which all architectures were evaluated, no graph model delivers a practically meaningful accuracy gain, and comparison against a margin fixed before analysis places them at parity or worse throughout; on the fourth, the fixed-adjacency model again degrades at every station.The failure is architecture-specific: only the fixed-adjacency model collapses in the heterophilous networks, a collapse neither the Spatio-Temporal Graph Convolutional Network (STGCN) nor Graph WaveNet reproduces.The problem lies in aggregation over a predetermined neighbourhood rather than in spatial encoding itself.The index ranks networks by the severity of that degradation but identifies no threshold below which aggregation becomes beneficial: a timestamped prediction to that effect was refuted.We present it as a preliminary diagnostic indicator for the architectures tested.

nodes.name: International journal of intelligent engineering and systems
FDUNet-LRSA: efficient frequency-adaptive segmentation for automated crop disease inspection
nodes.venue: Frontiers in Plant Science
nodes.abstract: The transition toward industrialized and automated agriculture requires reliable machine vision for high-throughput crop health monitoring and field decision support. Automated sweetpotato disease inspection, however, remains challenging because field images exhibit substantial variations in leaf scale, appearance, illumination, occlusion, and background complexity. Conventional U-shaped networks rely primarily on fixed convolutional kernels and local feature aggregation, whereas Transformer-based alternatives often introduce considerable computational overhead. This article proposes FDUNet-LRSA, a frequency-adaptive segmentation network that integrates frequency-domain dynamic convolution, low-resolution self-attention, and boundary-aware refinement. Frequency-domain dynamic convolution reconstructs input-dependent spatial kernels to improve feature adaptation under changing imaging conditions. Low-resolution self-attention captures long-range contextual dependencies in a fixed compact feature space, while boundary-aware refinement preserves irregular leaf contours during mask reconstruction. Under the reported evaluation protocol, FDUNet-LRSA achieved a mean test foreground IoU of 0.94 and a Dice coefficient of 0.97, with 3.72 GFLOPs. Additional experiments indicate that task-oriented moderate augmentation improves generalization compared with stronger augmentation. The proposed network provides an efficient visual perception approach for automated crop inspection systems.

nodes.name: Deep learning semantic segmentation of airborne LiDAR point clouds for urban flood inundation mapping: a case study of Hurricane Harvey, Harris County, Texas
nodes.venue: Journal of Applied Remote Sensing
nodes.abstract: Flood inundation mapping at the urban scale demands spatial resolution and geometric detail that satellite imagery alone cannot provide. Airborne LiDAR point clouds offer three-dimensional measurements of urban terrain and structures with centimeter-scale vertical accuracy, yet their application in deep-learning-based flood mapping remains underexplored. Most existing approaches rasterize point clouds into two-dimensional image channels, discarding the per-point geometric signal most informative for distinguishing flooded from non-flooded ground in complex urban environments. We present a fully LiDAR-based deep learning pipeline applied to the Hurricane Harvey flood event in Harris County, Texas, using post-event USGS 3DEP airborne LiDAR. A PointNet++ architecture with multi-scale grouping is trained for five-class semantic segmentation, classifying each point as flood ground, non-flood ground, building, vegetation, or others, directly on native point clouds. Using the Federal Emergency Management Agency (FEMA) Harvey Flood Depths Grid as ground truth, the model achieves a mean flood Intersection over Union (IoU) of 70% on spatially disjoint test tiles, with a best tile performance of 83%, providing the first published baseline for LiDAR-based flood segmentation with FEMA-validated labels. A comparison with Point Transformer v1 confirms that PointNet++ multi-scale grouping achieves superior flood detection. A feature ablation confirms that stable height-above-ground information is critical for building detection. Critically, the results demonstrate that label quality is the primary determinant of flood detection generalization. With FEMA-validated labels, the model achieves more than double the flood IoU compared with elevation-based proxy labels, regardless of architectural choices. The approach offers a scalable, geometry-based alternative to rasterized methods, with potential applications in rapid post-event flood assessment.

nodes.name: AI-Based Optimization Models for High-Performance Computing and Intelligent Network Architectures
nodes.venue: International Journal of Drug Delivery Technology
nodes.abstract: Artificial Intelligence (AI) has become a necessary technology to optimize High-Performance computers (HPC) systems and intelligent network architecture, such as optimizing the use of resources, the schedulization of workloads and network efficiency. This paper discusses how the three AI-based optimization tools, i.e., Deep Reinforcement Learning (DRL), Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) and Extreme Gradient Boosting (XGBoost) can be optimized to enhance performance in the HPC environment. It was done using a quantitative, simulation based, approach on the benchmark HPC workload and HPC network datasets. Data cleaning, feature selection, normalization and train-test splitting were used to preprocess the datasets and then model implementation and evaluation took place. The models were evaluated based on performance such as accuracy, precision, recall, F1-score, execution time, resource consumption, throughput, latency as well as the energy consumption. Experimental results demonstrated that the DRL model achieved the highest prediction accuracy of 96.8, 93.8 CPU resources consumption, 96.1 network efficiency, 12.8 Gbps throughput and 5.3 ms (lowest) network latency values. LSTM had the highest prediction accuracy of 95.2, and XGBoost had a score of 93.9 with the lowest training time rate of 39 minutes. The findings indicate that AI-based optimization is tremendously more effective regarding calculations and adaptability, scheduling, and resource allocation compared to the conventional ones. The suggested framework offers a viable solution to scalable, smart and energy efficient, intelligent HPC systems, which can be used to support next generations of computing and networking systems.

nodes.name: ADVANCED PROCESSING OF HIGH-RESOLUTION SAR CONSTELLATION IMAGERY FOR HURRICANE COASTAL IMPACTS
nodes.venue: ScholarWorks@UMassAmherst (University of Massachusetts Amherst)
nodes.abstract: Hurricane landfalls have far reaching impacts on coastal regions. The scale of the damage and dangerous conditions surrounding a storm can make it difficult to acquire in situ information about coastal conditions in the hours before, during, and after a landfall. New high resolution Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) satellite constellations provide the ability to rapidly acquire on-demand imagery of impacted regions regardless of cloud cover or time of day. This dissertation presents two applications of SAR satellite imagery for monitoring coastlines impacted by hurricanes. The first is a stereo radargrammetry algorithm which adapts the well-known Semi-Global Matching algorithm from optical to SAR images. The algorithm can be used to construct digital surface models (DSMs) of a coastline from SAR images from arbitrary viewing angles. The stereo algorithm is tested on a variety of coastal terrain types, and is demonstrated to be effective in measuring bare ground and vegetation heights, assisting in coastal change detection as well as generating up to date digital surface models useful for storm surge inundation modeling. The algorithm is found to be less effective at measuring surfaces in regions with rapidly changing surface feature heights such as urban regions. The second application uses subaperture SAR "video" series formed from long-dwell SAR spot- light images to infer coastal bathymetry through the measurement of wave fields. Several different methods of measuring wave field frequency and wavenumber are presented and evaluated on wave fields over simulated bathymetry, as well as real SAR images over a rocky coastline with steep bathymetry and a sandy coastline with shallow bathymetry. The algorithms are found to be able to successfully measure the wavenumber, but the short duration of the SAR "video" is found to produce inconsistent direct frequency estimates in the real imagery. It is found the most consistent bathymetry estimates are achieved when deep water is available in the SAR scene, allowing for the estimation of frequency through the inversion of the deep water wavenumber.

nodes.name: Wavelet-based adaptive image fusion of CT and MRI with local neighborhood variance for nasopharyngeal carcinoma
nodes.venue: Biomedical Physics & Engineering Express
nodes.abstract: Abstract Multimodal imaging of nasopharyngeal carcinoma (NPC) requires complementary representation of CT-derived bony anatomy and MRI-derived soft-tissue contrast. Existing fusion methods may fail to preserve both structural detail and soft-tissue information in a transparent and reproducible manner. We present a wavelet-based fusion framework that employs local neighborhood variance for adaptive weighting. This interpretable variance-driven strategy selectively integrates CT bony structures and MRI soft-tissue textures according to regional information content. The neighborhood configuration was selected through an ablation analysis of 232 clinical cases. Quantitative evaluation showed improved image-quality performance over the selected comparison methods across entropy, spatial frequency, average gradient, standard deviation, and edge information preservation factor, with respective gains of approximately 5.5%, 2.4%, 6.7%, 5.1%, and 3.2% relative to the best-performing baseline for each metric. These findings support the proposed method as an image fusion methodology for preserving complementary multimodal information; direct effects on target delineation, workflow efficiency, or dosimetric outcomes require future clinical validation.

nodes.name: Visual effects of urban environment art design based on composite Cycle Generative Adversarial Network
nodes.venue: Journal of Environmental Engineering and Landscape Management
nodes.abstract: In recent years, many regions have invested significant efforts in the in-depth study of artistic visual effects in urban environments to enhance the aesthetic appeal of urban districts. However, traditional visual optimization models are unable to refine image edges and textures, leading to distorted results. To optimize the artistic effects of urban district images, this study proposes a Cycle Generative Adversarial Network that incorporates a multi-head self-attention mechanism to enhance design. The network architecture is modified by adding multi-head self-attention modules. Spectral normalization is also introduced to improve the optimization process of both the generator and the discriminator. Finally, the images generated at different layers are concatenated, and the average of the extracted features is used as the output. The study compares the proposed network with publicly available datasets and commonly used optimization networks. The generated images achieve a pixel accuracy of 96.8% and a classification accuracy of 97.4%. In validation tests with a self-built dataset, the Peak Signal-to-Noise Ratio reaches 34.2 dB, outperforming the comparison models. In a comprehensive evaluation across various metrics, the Structural Similarity Index is 98.23% and the Visual Semantic Similarity is 96.78%. These results demonstrate that the proposed model analyzes images in various artistic styles and optimizes the visual effects of urban environments. It is beneficial for creating urban districts with distinctive artistic styles, enhancing the local cultural atmosphere, and attracting more domestic and international tourists.

Trustworthy AI for Sustainable Cities: A Multimodal Orchestration Agent-Based Framework for Civic Compliance
nodes.venue: Smart Cities
nodes.abstract: Sustainable municipal resource stewardship requires a harmonized artificial intelligence (AI) architecture that aligns technical performance with human-centered behavioral dynamics. Traditional smart city enforcement frameworks frequently trigger psychological reactance and perceptual failure in noisy, crowded urban spaces. This study presents HARMONY, a socio-technical edge-computing and agent-based framework that integrates localized computer vision (YOLOv8) with Mesa 3.0 agent modeling to promote non-coercive civic compliance in waste disposal. We formally calibrate behavioral constants, including the Politeness Modifier (Lp = 0.98), Gratitude Loop increment (δ = 0.025), and irreducible human defiance floor (ε = 0.12), grounded in self-determination theory, politeness theory, and empirical habit formation models. We also mathematically resolve sensory asymmetry in Hierarchical Orchestration Logic (HOL) by enforcing strictly normalized, bi-directional modality allocation (wv + wa = 1.0) conditioned on acoustic noise (N) and optical reliability (Qv). Across 100-run Monte Carlo simulations, HARMONY achieves a terminal Correct Disposal Rate (CDR) of 87.9% ± 3.3% (95% CI: [87.3%, 88.6%]), outperforming the coercive baseline (57.0% ± 4.9%). A comprehensive six-arm factorial ablation study isolates the distinct contributions of interactional politeness (+30.5% compliance gain), HOL sensory resilience (+1.6% to +21.4% under severe noise), and gratitude habituation (+0.5% to +30.3% sustained retention). Furthermore, population heterogeneity evaluations across diverse civic cohorts confirm robust performance from civic champions to highly resistant populations. Localized edge prototyping demonstrates 18.4 ms inference latency with 94.2% mAP, operating under an Edge-Only Ephemeral Vector Processing (E-EVP) paradigm that guarantees privacy-by-design. These findings demonstrate that cooperative, polite AI stewardship offers a scalable, legally robust, and ethically aligned alternative to punitive urban surveillance.

nodes.name: Tracing Sustainability Knowledge from Course Aims and Content to Learning Outcomes: An Element-Level Analysis of an Interior Architecture Curriculum
nodes.venue: Sustainability
nodes.abstract: Curriculum studies in sustainable design commonly map themes or Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs), but such mapping does not show whether specifically named disciplinary knowledge remains identifiable in formal learning outcomes. This study therefore examines how sustainability-related knowledge is represented across course aims/content and learning outcomes in a publicly documented 2025–2026 undergraduate Interior Architecture curriculum. Across all 70 course records, aims and content from 67 records yielded 1168 named knowledge elements; 169 sustainability-related elements in 17 courses met conservative inclusion criteria across seven domains. Each element was coded as preserved, generalized, displaced, or not represented. Independent re-unitization of a predefined 14-course validation sample yielded Krippendorff’s unitizing alpha of αU = 0.84, while independent recoding of all 169 included elements yielded 81.7% pre-adjudication agreement (Cohen’s κ = 0.725); final adjudicated transformation classifications were used for analysis. Overall, 45.0% were preserved at equivalent specificity, 30.2% generalized, 4.1% displaced, and 20.7% not represented. Preservation was highest for materials, water, resources, and circularity (77.8%) and indoor environmental quality, health, and safety (69.6%) but lower for climate/energy performance (22.2%) and heritage/adaptive reuse (20.7%). Leave-one-course-out estimates ranged from 41.1% to 48.3%. The study distinguishes curricular presence from outcome-level specificity and provides a transparent element-level diagnostic for examining how sustainability knowledge is formally recontextualized across curricular fields without treating documentary visibility as evidence of teaching or learning.

nodes.name: The Widening Cross-Country Food Availability Gap
nodes.venue: Foods
nodes.abstract: National food supplies have improved almost everywhere since 2000, yet progress towards Zero Hunger has stalled. This study examines how the cross-country distribution of food availability evolved and what contributed to its renewed widening, using the FAO indicator of average dietary energy supply adequacy. For 150 countries observed from 2001 to 2023, dispersion declined rapidly through the late 2000s, remained relatively stable until the mid-2010s, and subsequently increased. A continuous three-segment model outperforms both a two-segment V and a constrained plateau model (ΔAICc = 39.75 and 12.10, respectively) and is selected in 98.7% of three-year moving-block bootstrap samples. The three-phase pattern is also recovered from the latest FAOSTAT vintage, although historical revisions affect individual estimates. Most renewed widening occurs within geographic regions and subregions, while 93% of the 2013–2023 increase in the 90th–10th percentile gap originates below the median. Countries initially occupying the lowest adequacy quintile improved faster than those in the highest, but transition matrices provide no evidence of increasing mobility. Political stability and adequacy exhibit contemporaneous co-movement, although this association cannot be interpreted causally. Food-security monitoring should complement national and regional averages with distributional indicators that capture cross-country disparities. The concentration of renewed divergence within regions and in the lower half of the distribution suggests that food-security policies should target country-specific vulnerabilities rather than rely solely on broad regional classifications. In particular, tracking countries that persistently remain in or newly enter the lowest adequacy group could help prioritise support and better target food-security interventions. Overall, the findings highlight the importance of distribution-sensitive monitoring and policy approaches for advancing SDG 2 without assuming a universal turning year or a common trajectory across countries.

nodes.name: Synergistic Vacancy-Mediated Adsorption-Activation Strategy and Spatial Confinement Effect for Enhanced Electrochemiluminescence Sensing of Isocarbophos
nodes.venue: Analytical Chemistry
nodes.abstract: Abstract Exploring advanced strategies to overcome the sluggish activation kinetics of co-reactants and insufficient radical generation is pivotal for boosting electrochemiluminescence (ECL) sensing performance. Herein, an active radical-enriched ECL sensing platform for the ultrasensitive detection of isocarbophos (ICP) was fabricated by utilizing a synergistic vacancy-mediated adsorption-activation strategy coupled with a spatial confinement effect. Specifically, an oxygen-deficient titanium metal−organic framework (D-Ti MOF) was integrated as a robust co-reaction accelerator to trigger the emission of a pyrene-based hydrogen-bonded organic framework (PSA-HOF). Mechanistic studies revealed that abundant oxygen vacancies in D-Ti MOF served as catalytic sites, lowering the activation barrier of peroxydisulfate (K2S2O8) and promoting targeted adsorption and O−O bond cleavage to generate a high flux of sulfate radicals (SO4•−). Meanwhile, the porous MOF architecture imposed nanoscale spatial confinement, enriching reactive intermediates at the electrode interface and reducing diffusional loss. Such a confinement-enabled interfacial microenvironment was further substantiated by kinetic analyses, which revealed that D-Ti MOF promoted S2O82− reduction and redirected the process from predominantly diffusion-controlled behavior toward an adsorption- and confinement-coupled pathway, thereby increasing the local availability and productive utilization of reactive intermediates. Leveraging an isocarbophos-specific split aptamer recognition strategy, the proposed ECL biosensor exhibited a broad linear range (10 fM to 0.1 μM), an ultralow detection limit (8.38 fM), excellent stability, remarkable selectivity and reproducibility, making it highly applicable for practical sample monitoring. This work offers a new perspective for advancing co-reactant-based ECL biosensors and proposes a novel design strategy for ultrasensitive ECL sensing platforms.

nodes.name: SwinChange-DE: A Detail-Preserving Hierarchical Transformer Framework for High-Resolution Remote Sensing Image Change Detection
nodes.venue: Sensors
nodes.abstract: High-resolution remote sensing image change detection plays an important role in urban monitoring, disaster assessment, and land-cover analysis. However, complex spatial structures and diverse object scales make accurate change localization challenging, while progressive downsampling can obscure object boundaries and small changes. To address these challenges, this paper proposes SwinChange-DE, a detail-preserving hierarchical Transformer framework for high-resolution remote sensing image change detection. A Swin-inspired encoder extracts spatial–semantic representations at multiple resolutions through efficient contextual modeling. To bridge the semantic gap across feature levels, an adaptive fusion strategy refines shallow features under deep semantic guidance before aggregation. A detail enhancement module further leverages fused change information to guide the integration of high-resolution features from both temporal images during decoding, supporting boundary recovery and the detection of small-scale changes. Together, these components connect contextual representation, cross-scale alignment, and precise change localization within a unified framework. Extensive experiments were conducted on the LEVIR-CD+ and WHU-CD benchmarks. SwinChange-DE achieves F1-scores of 87.66% and 87.43%, respectively, outperforming the best-performing competing methods by 0.25% and 0.93% in F1-score. The results demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed framework in improving boundary delineation and recovering subtle changes in high-resolution remote sensing imagery.

nodes.name: SliceAutoMapi: High-throughput Automated Mapping of 2D Mouse Brain Image Slices to 3D Brain Volumes
nodes.venue: Journal of Innovative Optical Health Sciences
nodes.abstract: High-throughput spatial transcriptomics technologies such as MERFISH and Stereo-Seq generate massive brain sections requiring accurate registration to 3D reference atlases. However, existing methods face critical limitations. Manual tools lack scalability, feature-based methods suffer from anatomical landmark loss due to technical variability, and existing deep learning approaches are constrained by annotation scarcity and input size limits. Herein, we propose a ResNet-Transformer slice-to-volume registration method for accurate, high-throughput alignment of brain sections across coronal, sagittal, and horizontal orientations (SliceAutoMapi). Our approach leverages isotropic datasets to systematically generate multi-orientation training images, integrates ResNet for global feature extraction with Transformer for local and inter-slice spatial learning, and incorporates priors including slice spacing to improve slices registration efficiency. Experimental results demonstrate that our method achieves lower voxel and angle errors and a higher Dice coefficient on the controlled test set, validating its advantages for spatial transcriptomics applications. In conclusion, the hybrid ResNet- Transformer registration framework effectively addresses the core limitations of slice registration methods. It enables robust, high-throughput 3D atlas alignment for multi-plane brain sections and provides a reliable registration solution for large-scale brain tissue analysis.
